signature: moveTargetsToEnd(targetValue: number, nums: number[]) -> number[], the same values with every non-target element first, in original relative order, followed by every occurrence of targetValue
notes: Each input is [targetValue, nums], in the same order as the function's parameters, so the function can be passed to the harness directly. The problem is stated for zeros, but every approach takes the target as a parameter, so some cases use a non-zero target. `expected` is the whole array: unlike remove-occurrences-of-element, the tail is part of the answer and must hold exactly the moved targets. The inputs mirror remove-occurrences-of-element.json (expected here is its prefix followed by n - k copies of the target), plus the GeeksforGeeks examples. The two-pass and one-pass approaches mutate their argument and the naive one returns a new array, so assert the return value and pass a fresh copy of the input to each call.
